title: Task logs lose lines: a writer rewrites task.jsonl instead of appending; find it, prove it, fix it

chat.text: Three landing lines appended to task logs at 17:37 were gone from disk within 15 seconds; later Servex lines were written on top of the older content. Something holds a task log in memory and writes the whole file, or the merge script replaces a record file with a branch's older copy. A Sonnet task mastermind proves which with a test, fixes it so every task-log write is an append, recovers the lost lines from git, and guards it with the test.

message.text: Found it. At 17:38:07 the assistant-chain agent ran a plain `git merge --no-ff worktree/assistant-chain` in the main tree after merge.mjs gave it nothing useful. Git's merge saved the dirty tree as a stash commit (0283e997, 197 files), reset the whole tree to HEAD at 17:38:08, the merge failed, and git did not put the edits back. Your lost landing lines are in that commit, so they are recoverable. I am recovering them now, then adding a guard that blocks a plain `git merge` in the main tree.

Cause: an agent ran a plain `git merge --no-ff` in the dirty main tree at 17:38:07 after merge.mjs refused; git parked and hard-reset the tree, the put-back failed (Server/merge.mjs:563 was the same hazard in its no-overlap path). Test: `node Server/task-log-race.test.mjs` (13 checks, case 3 fails on the old merge.mjs). Recovered 301 lines, including the figma-to-code, model-switch and session-dup-check landing lines. Fix: git-guard blocks merge/pull/rebase/autostash in main, merge.mjs never runs git merge. Rule and mechanism: /framework/ai/sessions/doc/commit-rule.md
